summary: Sonatrach ordered 1,000 km of casing (21.7 bn DZD / USD 158.5M) from Sider El Hadjar's seamless-tube unit (TSS), split 292 km + 766 km, deliveries 2024-2026. TSS is the only seamless mill in the Maghreb (casing 6-16 in, 45,000 t/yr).
implication: TSS is the one named Algerian buyer of OCTG thread protectors. Protector origin, price and spec are UNKNOWN; call purchasing.

summary: El Hadjar began executing the Sonatrach contract and shipped 684 tubes on 12 trains to the oil fields.
implication: Confirms TSS is producing now, so protector consumption is real.

summary: Vallourec won a Sonatrach OCTG award worth more than USD 250M (deliveries 2025-2026) with VAM premium connections, made in Brazil, China, France and Indonesia.
implication: Most premium OCTG arrives already fitted with protectors, so the local protector market is limited to TSS output and re-protection or recycling (UNKNOWN).

summary: Sonatrach imported USD 731M of tubing in 2009-2010 while AMPTA (ex-TSS) workers struggled.
implication: Historic preference for imported tubulars; local share has risen since the 2023 contract.

summary: Alfapipe inaugurated a third pipe unit at Battioua (Oran) with 360,000 t/yr of welded steel pipe and a coating line, adding to Annaba and Ghardaia.
implication: Large-diameter line pipe needs bevel and end protection far beyond a 120 t press: a future-machine item only.

summary: Tosyali Algerie (Bethioua) exported 15,000 t of spiral tubes to Angola; capacity 300,000 t/yr; mega-pipe >1,300 mm.
implication: Same as Alfapipe: diameters exclude 120 t; possible coil/edge protector consumables (unverified).

summary: Searches for Alfapipe, Tosyali and Algerian OCTG plus 'thread protector' and 'protecteur filetage' returned only patents and US makers (Drilltec, MSI, Caplugs). No Algerian protector maker or importer surfaced.
implication: Absence of evidence. A local supplier may exist offline, so ask TSS directly.

summary: Sonatrach saved more than EUR 30M in one year by using nationally produced spare parts; partners first met in Feb 2022 now make high-quality parts; next step is electrical, electronic and more complex parts.
implication: The largest buyer actively substitutes imported spares, which is the entry lane for reverse-engineered plastic spares (plastic share UNKNOWN).

summary: Sonatrach's spare-parts inventory held more than 700,000 references; local content did not exceed 5% even though more than 50% of purchases were paid in dinars. Target: 55% of spares from local manufacturing.
implication: Structural import dependence for maintenance spares at the national oil company.

summary: 'Pieces de rechange: Sonatrach prospecte des prestataires locaux' plus pre-qualification notices for local designers and makers of precision mechanical spares.
implication: A formal channel exists: register as a local supplier and watch the pre-qualification notices.

summary: 81 exhibitors at the Hassi Messaoud technical days on mechanical, electrical and instrumentation manufacturing (Sonatrach local-content push).
implication: Exhibit at the next edition with a plastic spare-parts reverse-engineering offer.

summary: Sonelgaz signed two agreements for local manufacture of electrical equipment. SAIEG (ex-Rouiba lighting, AMC meters at El Eulma, MEI) makes switchboards in Oran and meters in El Eulma.
implication: Utility plastics (meter covers) are captive at SAIEG. Small panel parts may be outsourced (UNKNOWN).

summary: Sonelgaz exported meter spare parts to Tunisia, made by SAIEG at El Eulma.
implication: Meter plastics: KILL (captive).

summary: TSA: severe spare-parts shortage. Importers say their import files have been blocked for about two years, parts cost 2-4x their real price, and 96% of poll respondents say parts are hard to find. Counterfeit and smuggling risk. (Articles 'grave penurie' and 'la crise s'aggrave'; dates not visible.)
implication: Aftermarket plastic clips and fasteners may face the same shortage. Validate with aftermarket wholesalers; OEM supply stays KILL.

summary: More than 200 Algerian SMEs are said to be capable of supplying the car industry (plastic parts, seats, carpets, harnesses).
implication: Auto OEM supply is contested as well as policy-assigned to GPI.

summary: 7th SANIST reverse-subcontracting fair in Algiers: 70 exhibitors; focus on local manufacture of components, semi-products and spare parts.
implication: A venue to meet large buyers' spare-parts localisation managers.

summary: SOGEDIM lists a nylon PG09 IP68 cable gland at 50 DZD (another listing 35 DZD).
implication: Imported glands are cheap at retail, so the gland family is KILL for a 120 t start-up.

summary: SOGEDIM: Ø8 mm PP clip with nail, 2 DZD/pc (box of 100). Mabricole: round clips with steel nail, 200 DZD/100 (12 mm), 250 DZD/100 (14 mm), 300 DZD/100 (16 mm).
implication: Ex-works about 1-1.6 DZD: KILL without automated nail insertion.

summary: SOGEDIM: hammer-fix anchor 8x80 grey 15 DZD; plasterboard butterfly anchor 08 without screw 55 DZD. A search summary also cited a 100-box of 8x80 at 900 DZD (source page unclear).
implication: The butterfly anchor shows wide paper headroom. Confirm with wholesalers before treating it as a lead.

summary: French and Arabic searches for Condor/ENIEM spare-part shortages returned only French consumer sites and Algerian activity-code pages. No Algerian appliance-spare pain found online.
implication: Appliance spares stay INVESTIGATE; field check with repair shops in Tizi Ouzou, BBA and Setif.

summary: The Arabic search for unavailable plastic spare parts / factory stoppages in Algeria returned only auto-industry and GPI news, plus an Egyptian plastics-cluster article.
implication: No factory-downtime evidence online. Interviews with maintenance managers are needed.

summary: Solar 1000 MW tenders require at least 30% national integration. Junction boxes are about 6% of module cost, aluminium frames 10% and glass 16% (search summary). LONGi delegation met the PM in Apr 2025 on local panel production.
implication: The integration rule could pull local BOS plastics (clips, corners), but no named buyer asks for them.

summary: Creation of ENERGIA SUN SOLUTION, a company making PV-panel supports (headline).
implication: Possible buyer for rail end caps and clips; verify it is still active.

summary: Iris inaugurated an electronics complex in Setif (TVs, smartphones); the group also has a tyre complex.
implication: Possible small-housing and spacer buyer. No plastic-sourcing information found.
